prize_parts.citation: For incorporating firm heterogeneity into trade theory, showing how selection into exporting and reallocation across firms create new channels for the gains from trade.

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: B010 as a single part, credited to Melitz and Helpman. Round 1 did not change my view of the evidence. It sharpened the citation wording and the answer to the distinctness question, and that is the only change. The case rests on what I weigh most heavily, a mechanism that generates predictions that could have failed and were then confronted with data. Representative-firm new trade theory does not imply that exporters are a small, systematically more productive subset of firms, that entry and exit shift with trade costs, or that liberalisation raises industry productivity by reallocating activity within industries. Melitz (2003) implies all of these. Firm-level data from many countries have tested them, and the qualitative pattern has held for more than twenty years. On the chair's question about productivity distributions, my recollection is that the qualitative selection and reallocation result does not depend on the Pareto assumption, while the size of the welfare gains does. That is why I want the citation to reward the mechanism and not any welfare magnitude. Helpman's firm-level work, including Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exporting versus FDI, extends the mechanism into firm organisation across borders and justifies a second name. I would not cap the citation with a lifetime framing for Helpman. A multi-part configuration does not help under the three-person cap. B010 uses two names, and no other shortlisted part can be credited fairly with one name. A single part is therefore the cleanest proposal. This is a judgment on the contribution, not a head count. Eight members stating the same preference tells me the attribution is stable across assessors, nothing more.
statement.case_against: My strongest reservation is unchanged, and round 1 did not remove it. Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum and Hopenhayn are precursors or parallel contributors outside the credited pair, and Redding is omitted. Handling that through citation wording and the scientific background is a defensible choice, but it is a real cost. The magnitude of the selection gains depends on parametric assumptions, so a citation that implied settled welfare numbers would overreach. Field balance after the 2008 trade prize remains a legitimate consideration, though I do not think it should override merit. I also take seriously that B019 is conceptually foundational with a cleaner two-name credit line, and that my preference for B010 rests partly on how I weigh evidential testability against mechanism clarity. Others may weigh these differently. I rely on my own recollection of these literatures and have not independently verified the record.

responses.point: Boppart keeps B019 first for its single-mechanism, two-author attribution. He treats B010 as a serious alternative but flags credit disputes with Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum. He also says his preference is a judgment between two strong candidates and not a claim that B010 is weaker on merit.
responses.response: I appreciate that framing, because it is close to my own view of B019. The remaining difference is how much weight to give clean attribution against the depth of the evidence. A two-name credit for Kiyotaki and Moore is cleaner than ours, and I concede that. My doubt is about testability. The collateral-amplification channel is harder to identify directly than the theory's influence suggests, and the chair's question to you about the strongest direct evidence is the right one. If you can point to it, I would update toward B019. On the precursor point, I would answer by wording the B010 citation narrowly around selection and reallocation and by acknowledging the exporter-fact and Eaton-Kortum strands in the background, not by widening the laureate set. Given the cap, that is also why I do not see a workable two-part configuration.

responses.point: Strömberg ranks B019 first but says he is not fully settled on the order of B019 and B010. He sees B010 as having broad agreement and an equally clean attribution, and as possibly the safer case. He distinguishes the 2022 prize on banks and runs from Kiyotaki-Moore's collateral-and-asset-price feedback.
responses.response: I agree with the 2022 distinction on mechanism, and I would not say B019 is excluded by it. I do not rank B010 higher because it is safer. Safety is about the likely reception of a prize, not about the science, and I do not count it as merit. My reason is that the selection and reallocation predictions are specific and could have been rejected by firm-level data, and they were not. The collateral channel has influenced the field greatly, but the evidence tying it to amplification in the data is more indirect. If the Committee judged that distinction less important than the single-mechanism clarity you stress, that would be a reasonable reading. Your move to the two-name set also removes the Gertler problem that would otherwise have weighed on B019 for me, so the credit comparison is now closer than it was in round 1.

responses.point: Enflo prefers B032 with Autor, Hanson and Dorn. She argues that the causal evidence on local labour-market adjustment has been stress-tested for a decade and reaches beyond trade models. She narrowed from Katz to the trade-shock core after discussion.
responses.response: I give weight to credible causal evidence, and I ranked B032 eighth, so I do not dismiss it. Narrowing to the trade-shock core is a sensible response to the overlap with recent prizes and to the mixing of strands in the ballot entry. The remaining difficulty for me is what the discovery is. The China-shock papers establish slow and costly regional adjustment, but magnitudes and long-run persistence depend on shift-share identification that is still debated. I agree with you that debate over magnitudes is not in itself evidence of fragility. For B010 the qualitative predictions have held up across many datasets and countries, and the disagreement is mainly about size. For B032 the disagreement is partly about what the evidence shows. I would also say it is harder to draft a three-name citation without choosing between the trade-shock and task-framework strands, which you acknowledge.

responses.point: Hassler, as chair, supports the Helpman-Melitz pair with a narrow citation and no lifetime framing. He treats Redding as a later quantitative extension and not part of the core. He also asks whether the committee wants a methods or discovery framing for B003, while ranking it as his strongest alternative.
responses.response: I agree on the narrow wording and on keeping Redding out of the core. His main contribution is quantitative and spatial trade built on this framework, which is a real extension and not a co-origin. I have shortened my citation accordingly and kept it to selection, reallocation and the gains from trade, with no claim over trade theory generally. On B003, I would want the committee to decide first whether it is rewarding a substantive discovery about market power and welfare or a set of estimation methods. Until then, I would keep it behind B010 because the Bresnahan, Reiss and Benkard boundary is still open. I note as a disclosure point that you are the chair and one of the eight B010 supporters, so I read our agreement as independent attribution judgments and not as a committee verdict.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee accepts a two-name citation that omits Redding and the Bernard-Jensen-Eaton-Kortum-Hopenhayn strands, and whether acknowledgment in the scientific background is adequate for those omissions.

Whether my recollection is right that the qualitative selection and reallocation result is robust to non-Pareto productivity distributions while the welfare magnitudes are not. I have not verified this against sources.
Whether the Committee sees B010 as clearly distinct from the 2008 new trade theory prize, and how much field balance should count.
Whether direct evidence for the B019 collateral-amplification channel is stronger than I recall. If it is, my ordering of B010 and B019 could change.
Whether the B003 laureate set (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes versus a wider group) can be settled, since that affects its standing as an alternative.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to Helpman, Melitz or the other credited names on B010, B019 or B001 is apparent from my supplied profile, and I have not independently verified that beyond the profile. For transparency, I disclose my SSE affiliation shared with Andersson, Friberg and Strömberg, and my long co-authorship with Magnus Johannesson, a former Committee member (2016-19 per the profile), who is not a candidate. I also disclose my Institute for Replication, Brodeur and Harvard evolutionary-dynamics ties, none of which involve a shortlisted candidate. As a metascience researcher I may weigh testability and replication evidence more heavily than colleagues from other fields do, and I flag that as a possible bias. These are disclosed and not adjudicated.
